reforms.description: The Canadian government plans to enhance the efficiency of the transportation network by revising outdated regulations and investing in the Canadian Network for the Advancement of Research, Industry and Education (CANARIE) to create a high-speed experimental communications network aimed at helping innovative companies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving transportation efficiency and investing in research infrastructure are vital for supporting innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Plans for investment and regulatory changes have been publicly stated.
reforms.importance_rationale: The investment in CANARIE and regulatory revisions represent significant but not transformative changes.
reforms.source_quote: Increased funding will be provided for the Canadian Network for the Advancement of Research, Industry and Education (CANARIE) which is charged with, among other things, creating a high speed experimental communications network.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions 'investing in the Canadian Network for the Advancement of Research, Industry and Education (CANARIE)' which relates to research infrastructure.

reforms.description: The Canadian government has implemented tax incentives and grants to stimulate private sector R&D spending while reviewing its major R&D support programme, the Scientific Research and Experimental Development tax incentive, to enhance its effectiveness. Additionally, proposals have been outlined to link various economic development instruments to improve innovation performance across sectors, particularly for small businesses.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to enhance private sector R&D investment and innovation, which are critical for economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The tax incentives and grants have been put into effect, and the strategy has been officially adopted.
reforms.importance_rationale: The implementation of tax incentives and a comprehensive strategy for innovation represents a significant overhaul of the R&D support system.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government's major R&D support programme, the Scientific Research and Experimental Development tax incentive, came under review in the last Budget.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform discusses 'tax incentives and grants to stimulate private sector R&D spending' which qualifies as an innovation instrument.

reforms.description: The federal government reviewed and restricted the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit programme in 1995, excluding banks and financial institutions from claiming credits and circumscribing claims for computer software and hardware upgrades to refocus the programme on cutting-edge technology development.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The restriction of SR&ED credits to exclude financial institutions and limit software/hardware claims may reduce incentives for some R&D investment, but refocusing on cutting-edge technology development could improve allocative efficiency and support higher-impact innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'reviewed and restricted' in past tense, indicating implementation in 1995.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant narrowing of an existing major tax credit programme affecting eligibility and scope, but not a structural overhaul of the innovation support system.
reforms.source_quote: One change is that banks and other financial institutions will not be able to collect federal research and development tax credits pending a government review of the entire programme. A major concern is the claiming of tax credits for upgrades to computer software and hardware, including customising off-the-shelf software programmes.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform involves a review of the 'Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit programme' which is an innovation instrument.

reforms.description: Youth Internship Canada provides federal seed funding to encourage industry and education institutions to develop structured pathways from school to emerging and expanding sectors, combining in-class with on-the-job training based on industry-determined skill standards.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Building human capital through structured training pathways aligned with industry skill standards enhances the supply of skilled workers for emerging sectors, supporting productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text uses present tense 'provides', indicating the programme is in operation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant programme combining federal funding with industry-education partnerships to develop talent pipelines, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: Under Youth Internship Canada, the federal government provides seed funding to encourage industry and education institutions to develop structured pathways from school to emerging and expanding sectors of the economy.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform provides 'seed funding to encourage industry and education institutions' which relates to human capital for R&D.

reforms.description: The Canadian Government announced innovation products and initiatives to promote SME participation in global markets, including the Business Networks Strategy to encourage cooperation among small businesses and the Canadian Technology Network to help firms design and market globally competitive products.
reforms.component_name: SME export development and innovation products
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supporting SME participation in global markets through business networks and technology networks enhances market access, competitive positioning, and technology adoption, supporting productivity and growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text explicitly states 'announced innovation products and initiatives'.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant initiative combining multiple strategies to support SME competitiveness and market participation, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: Recently-announced government initiatives will amplify or complement those launched previously, which included proposals to encourage co-operation among small businesses to help achieve the critical size needed to compete in international markets (The Business Networks Strategy) and to bring together small firms to design and market globally competitive products (Canadian Technology Network).
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions 'initiatives to promote SME participation in global markets' which supports the startup ecosystem for R&D-intensive firms.

reforms.description: The Canadian government has implemented tax credits and grants as primary instruments to encourage private sector R&D spending, aiming to stimulate innovation and enhance industrial performance. Additionally, a strategy has been outlined to improve Canada's innovation performance by linking various economic development instruments into a coherent agenda, focusing on expanding markets, encouraging small business growth, and promoting science and technology across all sectors. A federal Science and Technology Strategy is also intended to streamline support for innovation and ensure it is conducive to private sector growth, particularly among small businesses.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to stimulate R&D spending and enhance industrial performance, which are expected to raise productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canadian government has implemented tax credits and grants as primary instruments.
reforms.importance_rationale: The implementation of tax credits and grants as well as a coherent strategy for innovation represents a significant structural change in the innovation policy landscape.
reforms.source_quote: The Government has recently outlined a number of proposals to make the economy more innovative and productive.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform discusses 'tax credits and grants as primary instruments to encourage private sector R&D spending' which qualifies as an innovation instrument.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The federal government announced a comprehensive reduction in business subsidies and support programmes in 1997, with Industry Canada winding down 43 of its 54 subsidy and support programmes by fiscal year 1997/98, reducing its budget by over 40 per cent (C$0.5 billion), though science and technology support expenditure cuts were relatively limited.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Reducing inefficient business subsidies and support programmes can improve allocative efficiency and reduce market distortions, though the relatively limited cuts to science and technology support preserve investment in innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text indicates programmes were to be wound down 'by fiscal year 1997/98', suggesting legislative decision in 1997 with implementation to follow.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: A major structural reform involving the elimination of 43 of 54 programmes and a 40 per cent budget reduction across Industry Canada, representing a significant system-wide reorientation of government support.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Industry Canada will wind down all but 11 of its 54 subsidy and support programmes by the fiscal year 1997/98. Its budget will decline by C$ 0.5 billion over this period, a cut of over 40 per cent.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description discusses a reduction in business subsidies and support programmes without a clear focus on R&D funding.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Canadian Government presented the Building a More Innovative Economy (BMIE) strategy in November 1994, a comprehensive industrial strategy with over 55 commitments to action across fifteen federal departments and agencies, focusing on promoting a healthy marketplace, strengthening infrastructure, exploiting trade opportunities, and improving technology and innovation diffusion throughout the economy, particularly in SMEs. This strategy was supported by a commitment to complete a Science and Technology Review to provide recommendations on how the federal government could play a more effective role in developing and commercializing scientific and technological advances, and an intention to release a federal Science and Technology Strategy in fall 1995 aimed at streamlining and reviewing government support programmes for science and technology.
all_reforms_including_excluded.package_name: Building a More Innovative Economy (BMIE) Strategy
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The BMIE strategy aims to improve technology and innovation diffusion, strengthen infrastructure, and promote a healthy marketplace, which should enhance productivity and allocative efficiency across the economy, particularly for SMEs.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The BMIE strategy was presented in November 1994; the Science and Technology Review and Strategy were announced as future commitments (fall 1995), indicating the overall package was announced but implementation details were still being developed.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: A major structural reform involving a comprehensive industrial strategy with over 55 commitments across fifteen federal departments and agencies, representing a system-wide reorientation of government support for innovation and technology diffusion.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: In November 1994, the Government of Canada presented in a report entitled Building a More Innovative Economy (BMIE) a comprehensive industrial strategy designed to increase Canada's international competitiveness so that the private sector can create jobs and raise the standard of living of Canadians. The strategy rests on a four-pronged approach which focuses on promoting a healthy marketplace, strengthening Canada's physical and telecommunications infrastructure, exploiting internal and external trade opportunities, and improving the development and diffusion of technology and innovation throughout the economy (particularly in SMEs).
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description is too vague and does not clearly indicate a specific reform related to R&D funding or knowledge transfer.
